 in CMA.No.481/2018 by Aanj) .. Appellant
 Versus
 1.Munisamy
 2.Selvaraj .. Re
 Prayer : Civil Miscellaneous Appeal filed under Section 173 of Motor
 Vehicles Act, 1988 against the Judgment and Decree of the Motor Accident
 Claims Tribunal (Ii Additional District Judge) at Puducherry made in
 M.C.O.P.No.1017 of 2007 dated 01.10.2013.

For Appellant : Mr.G.Venkatesan
 For Respondents : Mr.B.Balavijayan
 Judgment

The Civil Miscellaneous Appeal has been filed against the Judgment and Decree of the Motor
Accidents Claims Tribunal (Ii Additional District Judge) at Puducherry made in M.C.O.P.No.1017 of
2007 dated
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
2.The manner of the accident, factum of the accident, rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle are not in dispute 3.

On 27.01.2007, the deceased first appellant was involved in levelling road, the tractor with trailor which was used for carrying sand for the purpose of levelling rad came and ran over the appellant causing injuries, fractures.
Hence, the claim petition.
4. The appellants are the claimants seeking to challenge the award passed by the Tribunal on the ground of quantum.
The respondents 2 and 3 are the owner of the offending vehicle.
For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per their ranking before the trial Court.

Ezappan (Died) vs Munisamy on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73686798/
1 5.
During the trial before the Tribunal, the first appellant was examined as PW1.
Ex.P1 to P7 were marked.
Ex.P1 is the FIR Copy, Ex.P3 is the Accident Inspection Report, Ex.P4 to P7 are the discharge slips.

The Tribunal on consideration of both oral and documentary evidences came to conclusion that the accident has taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis driver of the offending vehicle, accordingly, fixed the liability to both the respondent and granted the compensation as tabulated below:

Calculation Rs.
 Partial Permanent Disability Rs.15,000/-
 Pain and sufferings Rs.15,000/-
 Extra nourishment Rs.5,000/-
 Travelling expenses Rs.3,000/-
 Loss of Income Rs.6,000/-

Total compensation is hereby fixed at Rs.44,000/-
6.Heard
Mr.B.Balavijayan, learned counsel for the appellants and Mr.B.Balavijayan, learned counsel for the Respondents and perused the materials placed on record.

7. Considering the facts and also taking note of the plea raised by the learned counsel for the appellant, this Court is of the considered view that the income of the deceased should be fixed at Rs.6000 for three months [(i.e., 6000x3=Rs.18,000/-] and the same is hereby enhanced;

further,
pain and sufferings is enhanced at Rs.20,000/-, extra nourishment is enhanced at Rs.8,000/- and similarly travelling expenses is also enhanced at Rs.5000/-.

It is seen in the award that the attender charges was not granted to the claim https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis petitioner, however, this Court is hereby granting the attender charges to the claim petitioner as Rs.500 per day for seven day, i.e., 500x7=Rs.3500.

Accordingly, the award amount is modified as below:
 Calculation Rs.
 Partial Permanent Disability Rs.15,000/-
 Pain and sufferings Rs.20,000/-
Extra nourishment Rs.8,000/-

Travelling expenses Rs.5,000/-
 Loss of Income Rs.18,000/-
 Attender charges Rs.3,500/-

Total compensation is hereby fixed at Rs.69,500/-
 10.

In fine,
(i) this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal stands partly allowed to the extent indicated above.

Accordingly,
the compensation awarded is enhanced from Rs.44,000/- to Rs.69,500/-.
The rate of interest awarded by the Tribunal remains in tact.
No Costs.

within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order, less the amount, if any already deposited. https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis (iii)
